reviews.text: Great concept, not fun in its current form. I really love the idea of the game, the board as skill tree, but it needs more. As is, there is nothing else on the board, no obstacles, no power-ups , just the skill tree and monsters. You don't have a dash or or shield or any kind of "Oh sht!" button, so all you can do is run around, basically in circles, kiting the enemies to try and get them away from the next circle you want to unlock. There doesn't seem to be any kind of advanced pathing for the bad guys, they just run at you and constantly get cheap hits, and after a few minutes they just swarm you and you die. Maybe you can get powerful enough to melt them, but with 6 hours of gameplay I never felt close. I actually wonder if the enemies' health is scaling with your power, because it just doesn't feel like they get any easier to kill, despite my (supposedly) getting more and more powerful. On top of that, I don't find the complete lack of instruction to be a fun design choice. I have no idea what the pink or blue stats mean, or what several of the big unlocks on the skill boards do, and I don't know any way of figuring it out besides googling it, and that seems like some pretty lazy/bad game design that's being passed off as some kind of artistic choice. <Eye roll.> Just tell me what the powers do, I shouldn't have to do homework to play your game. Hope the game gets a major overhaul to make it more fun, because otherwise it's a lot of wasted potential.

"There is no tutorial, and no text; it will be up to you to experiment and discover synergies!" If you want people to properly experiment and buildcraft, you will need to give more info on what things actually do somewhere. I kind of like that the game doesn't explain a bunch of stuff ingame, but it needs some sort of catalog / codex / whatever you want to call it where it actually tells you what does what. It can be an option in the main menu and all the info can only unlock once you've used the item / synergy ingame, but give us the info somewhere, somehow. Other than that, gameplay is good, graphics are stylish, sound design is good too. But give us some form of info somewhere so we can truly work on builds, like we can in the games that this competes with.

(EDIT 2/11/26: It's just not fun to be honest. Looking back at the review it wasn't worth all that) I started out extremely positive on the game but after playing a couple hours, I cannot recommend it in its current state The music is incredible, let's get that out of the way: Absolute bangers, every track. The issues come from being way too married to its own ideas to the point its a detriment. The lack of Sigil explanation/Text is a good idea, it trusts in the player's basic intelligence. The problem is, the Sigils for Passive Abilities outside of Skills and Weapons are in many cases indecipherable and are needlessly esoteric. Likewise, the Gameboy aesthetics are great, it really gives that Link's Awakening feel. But in the later game, the lack of color turns things into a Visual Nightmare that makes it impossible to tell whats going on and the vast majority of Damage I'm taking is from enemies I physically CANNOT SEE due to being covered up by the white effects of my own attacks. The game is in early access, there's enough quality here that I have no doubt it'll get sorted out. But as of right now, playing this game might legitimately give some people a headache. "Accessibility Options" isn't just a buzzword used by people who can't beat Elden Ring/Dark Souls, sometimes they're needed

优点：很有创意的把战斗地图和天赋树结合了，好了没了，以下全是缺点 也可以当对照翻译看： 缺点： 1.属性是什么？？？ 谁能看得懂这些图标都什么意思啊？各个属性都是干嘛的？？？以下是我的实验出来的东西 1力量、2敏捷、3智力、4回血、5护甲、6闪避、7射程、8暴击、9攻速、10吸取范围、11幸运、12移速、13火、14雷、15冰、16眩晕、17毒、18附加伤害 有那么多的属性需要玩家去猜是干嘛的，过于离谱，而且哪怕猜到是干什么的，我也依然不知道具体加成是多少，1点攻速和1点攻击范围对应具体多少数值，我到通关了都不知道 - 2.特殊被动是什么？？？ 抛开属性图标后，特殊技能的图标就更离谱了，很多都是你不选一遍根本不知道有什么用的，更多的甚至是选完了打完一把都不知道有什么用离谱 以下是比较好用的： （1）开宝箱不花钱，图标是宝箱加一个碎掉的钱，出门3步有这个直接毕业这把乱杀 （2）升级返3块钱，图标是升级图标加3个钱的图标，前期的皇帝 （3）杀怪掉钱，图标是怪物骷髅头加钱的图标，看起来是给0.2块，具体不知道 （4）物理转魔法（不是），图标是A属性指向BC属性，后期的皇帝 其他的？看不懂，也不知道有什么用，选了就是一整把没有存在感，离谱 - 3.主动技能怎么这么垃圾？？？ 虽然没有文字说明，作者还是贴心的给每个武器左边都标了属性加成，右边都标了射程和穿透 但是！但是！但是！！！ 怎么会有一个幸存者游戏，一半技能都是打你面朝方向的？？你玩个战士拿拳头主C打个一把能不吐出来找我，更不要说还有斧子这种根据你的拖拽进行攻击的逆天玩意 推荐技能： （1）剑，攻击方式为砍2刀后第三下绕自身一周，完美aoe技能 （2）卡牌，攻击方式为丢出5张卡牌，超高攻速对单无敌，前期的皇帝 （3）三只箭，局外成长点出，攻击方式是生成3只箭，召唤出时有碰撞伤害清怪很强 - 4.光！污！染！ 我！看！不！清！怪！ 游戏中期开始特效堆的疑似刚打完辐光出来，怪物死亡特效、武器命中特效、角色模型，全是一个颜色，根本看不出来我是谁我在哪我要往哪躲，莫名其妙就会被加速怪撞掉10血，你就玩吧 - 5.地图与怪的交互 刚刚不说地图是优点吗？站在地图上1秒的加点方式确实创新，但当你玩个5分钟之后，就开始发现，满屏幕的小怪堵着你，你根本就加不上点，然后就是清不动怪被更多的怪堵路滚雪球。天赋树、怪物、角色、角色弹道又都是一个颜色，你根本就看不清天赋树点到哪了，以及这个点加没加上，总之就是痛苦 刚刚打完无尽模式出来，后期捡经验卡的没边，怪物和角色疑似都不会成长，没什么意思，无后续更新的话不作推荐

I'd like to start out by saying, at it's core, it's a fun twist on the roguelite bullet hell genre. That said, there are many design choices that really hamper my enthusiasm, and not because of how the core gameplay is, but how it just makes it less enjoyable to play and explore the possible build diversity. The reason for this is, there is no text for pretty much anything in the game. None. The options menu, the skill tree board, your weapons, nothing other than some numbers, that don't even have what unit of measure they're in. (the delay on firing a weapon appears to be in seconds, but I'm still not sure of that. Worse, the color yellow.... EVERYTHING is yellow. Your character. The gameboard. Your attacks/spells. Explosions. EXP/Money pickups. And it's the exact same shade of yellow - just slightly less brighter than our sun. After 20 minutes my eyes start to feel fatigued, both by the color choice, and the inability to discern the different things happening on the screen from one another. Kill an enemy, a yellow swirly thing flys around you - cool, except I can't tell if it's money following me, or an enemy. Shoot a weapon. Not sure it's an enemy or my own attack..... All yellow, all the same yellow. There is one colored thing of note - your health bubble above your character... It's red, and eyecatching, and it's what you'll likely start to perceive as your character when things get frantic - You'll start to track it with your eyes to dodge the yellow all around you - too bad, it's not your hitbox - that's below, and worse, to the left of your hp bubble, making you have to search for your character in the sea of urine colored bliss. The enemies - in a lot of bullet hells, they have spawns that if you're careful, you can avoid trapping yourself. You'll find a hole to fit through by doubling back sometimes. Not here. They spawn seemingly whatever direction your facing, and behind simultaneously... and when your finally getting a bead on them, a wave of 3x as fast enemies start spawning to get to you before you break out of the ring of death. And, they always seem to be in the way of wherever you're going - need a node - they're already there because you ran from there to keep out of the pincer attack.... but you have no where to goto, they're everywhere. Lastly, as was firstly, the icons have no text for skill points. While some are industry regulars (sword for attack, fist for strength, wizard hat for intellect, lightning bolt, fire, snowflake, and such), the rest are just weird - there's like a blue door-ish thing? A pink thing that looks kinda like diglet if you squint, 3 stars thing, then there's 3 swords, red, grey, and bluegreen... and those are just the common perk points - not the major nodes with the hieroglyphs. So, yeah, it could be a really good game, but man, is it ever frustratingly flawed, in my opinion, on design choices that to me make 0 sense - I get you like the monochrome aesthetic, but this is not the type of game that works well with. Do us, and yourself a favor, and forego the art project, for game design, respectfully.

Very cool idea and overall well executed. I can't get over there is no text in the game though. I really dislike not knowing what anything means and not being able to make an informed decision. I totally respect this might appeal to some but unfortunately it's not for me.

It's passable and fine for a couple hours, but the choice to not have any text in the game leaves the game a challenge to recommend. I don't know how to evaluate if some unlock is good and what to pick up without a lot of trial and error and it just gets exhausting over time. The game basically becomes brute force through levels a bunch of times until you can buy the permanent meta upgrades... which you also have no clue what they mean or do, but I assume they make you start stronger by default? I want to make meaningful choices I want to go "I should buy these upgrades because I want these kinds of weapons, and these icons mean things that help me" but I don't know what "98 Bow" means on a weapon, how is that different than "05 Bow With 3 Arrows" and does it have anything to do with "40 Sword + 05 Blue Sword with a +" and how does that work with "+80% Fist"? Some are more obvious like the magnet is pickup range, and the arrows in a circle is cooldown reduction, and there's the Fire/Lightning/Ice magic damage types. But It's hard to parse how strong any individual purchase is like how much stronger does "5 Fire" make me? Basically I don't know how to evaluate what is even good or what anything does without trial and error and it just gets exhausting. Otherwise it's passable but I can't recommend it without the game putting a guide of some kind in the game so you know what things mean.
no tooltips at all

I *really* like this turn on the survivors like genre. Having points you have to contest to get stronger instead of just, running away until you get strong enough to sit still is far more appealing to me. I'm only a handful of runs in, and I'll probably come update my review when I get further, but I'm just really, really enjoying playing a few runs of this before work every day so far.

I am heavily biased toward show, don't tell gameplay these days. I don't want to sit through hours and hours of exposition dumping, tooltips, or have to read a f***ing manual to understand how a game's mechanics work. I want to FAFO, and I love this game for it. Is it difficult at the start, since there's NO tooltips, explanation, or text of any kind to show what you're picking up and what it does? ABSOLUTELY. Because the game is forcing you to figure it out for yourself, to find what works and use intuition, rather than explanation, to determine what the sigils mean. Give the game a chance. I only have five hours in it and I've already cleared runs based on what I've learned. It's five dollars. People pay more for games that do a lot less. Also, your currency is a cool S, and you can't ever go wrong with a cool S.
Well crafted, good sound-ing, phenomenal, stylish, unique... ...way to not translate a game to any language. Game is pretty fun too though.
I wouldn't recommend this game until it has some sort of information/tooltip for the unlocks, I have no idea what im unlocking or how it effects my build.

Its a drug for first several hours, wildly innovative for vampire survivor genre, but at some point you hit a wall. There are like 4 types of enemy that differenciate only by speed, hp and spawn direction, and eventually theyll just choke you out, like this game is being chocked by dedication to its gimmicks. You can decipher what some special nodes do through trial and error, but most of the stuff is an unnoticeable stat upgrade. One color pallete is hard to read at times. Theorethically you should be planning path and trying risky builds, but you mostly just get owerwhelmed by horde running in circles. I wish abilities were stronger and had bigger hitboxes, because it always feels like enemies are getting past you and surround you.

this game, truly a gem of the genre, succeeds in an area where all the other survivor-likes ive played have failed: it actually feels like there is room for skill and strategy, beyond merely your choice of weapons. it does this by putting a big emphasis on positioning. instead of mindlessly kiting huge packs of enemies around, you're constantly thinking about which direction to move on the skill tree, and occasionally abusing the pathfinding to create slim openings to activate a node. not to mention how many of the weapons have directionality as well!
This game is fun. Great meta progression system and gameplay.
A fine survivor-like from Achromi.

I know the lack of tooltips/tutorials/anything instructional at all is part of the magic of this game (kind of like Brotato pre-codex days), but I feel the eventual addition of a codex made that game so much better. Just a bit of description (can even be vague and leave things out) would go a long way to make this really good game a great game ^_^

This is a highly conditional endorsement. Skigill is a bullet heaven in the mold of Vampire Survivors. However, it definitely makes its own path. The key difference is the power-ups are literally on the game board and you walk on them to get them. It's a good mechanic, and probably the best thing about the game. However, there are design decisions that make it hard to endorse. 1. Gameplay can be pretty opaque. There is absolutely no explanation given for what the icons mean. Most of them make sense pretty quickly (the flame increases your fire damage, for example), but some of them might be entirely unguessable. Fortunately, there are websites that document them all, so a quick perusal will resolve those questions. 2. Color choices, or the lack thereof. It can be pretty challenging, especially late-game when there are hordes of enemies, to figure out what's going on. This is common for bullet heavens, but Skigill's monochromatic pallette, and no ability to filter out weapon effects, mean that late-game you better trust your weapon combo, because you sure won't be able to see what's going on. 3. The difficulty curve feels pretty high at the start. I did manage to get over it, but for a while, I felt like I was getting absolutely no progress. And in the end, I wasn't sure I had fun doing it. And what's the point of the game if not to have fun? In short, I'm not sure I had fun figuring out Skigill's quirks, but it does execute on it's core premise. For the price, it's worth experimenting with if you like bullet heavens, just be prepared for some frustration around the design of the game.

pretty underwhelming. most game elements are represented by symbols and numbers, not text, and never explained. its very trial and error, try every spell, but most felt weak and useless, some are frustrating to aim or have clunky animations. you just walk in circles killing enemies. upgrading spells doesn't change them much aside from damage and cooldown, no unique feeling of powering up, just bigger numbers. some things just feel lazy, like the color pallette, everything is yellow - enemies, exp, spell effects, your character, damage numbers that only appear over the same yellow enemies, the path and nodes... but maybe appreciated by others. probably never finding out if this one "gets good eventually"
fun
Visual clarity is terrible (all yellow), no descriptions for anything so you have to guess what items and upgrades do. Reasonable game loop, but in an oversaturated space it doesn't stand out.

I bought this because I was a fan of Master Key. I've never played a bullet hell type of game before but found this very enjoyable. The music is so good! Pay close attention to how upgrades affect stats and abilities to better figure out what the symbols mean. Some symbols I couldn't figure out and had to Google lol I've only unlocked two characters so far! Despite so much yellow, I have only lost sight of my character once. Thought I'd add his here since the yellow scheme seems to bother some people but personally, no real issue.

I had a lot of fun playing Skigill. The presentation and method of progression is unique. Many people complain about the lack of help and text since this game uses only simple icons to give you clues. It isn't some mind-bending puzzle to figure out though. A few hours and a little patience and possibly a small bit of trial and error is all it takes to understand.
One of the most interesting and fun bullet heavens I've played. Fun to decipher, incredibly satisfying to do well at, and overall just incredibly unique
A little slow, but decent gameplay loop, meta progression, and aesthetics for a pixel game.

This is very good, especially considering the price. A classic survivor with a twist, as the concept of unlocking zones to get power-ups has been stretched to the maximum since unlocking zones is literally how you make your build, with the powerups layed out on the map as in a skill tree. The game is honestly pretty nice-looking, musics are a good notch above what I expected in terms of quality for a little game of that size and prize. Is it the best game in its genre that will ever have been made? Definitely no. But it's a nice concept, well executed, definitely well worth its price. Playing it on linux mint on an oldish (around 10yo model) laptop, works flawlessly out of the box.
Simple mechanics with surprising depth!

Very fun game! Got almost 30 hours of gameplay time till I 100% it. Definitely recommended if you enjoy rouguelike-vampire survivors-dodging crap type of games. Biggest downside (maybe subjective, but still relevant IMO) is lack of information - there arent really any descriptions, so you kinda have to guess/figure out what "icon" means and modifies what (or use a guide). Now that I think of it, it has bit of Dark Souls vibes as there is very little hand holding in terms of information.
Very unique idea, pretty fun. The monochromatic art is eye-catching but it makes readability of the playfield pretty poor. Very excited to see this one after some more time in the oven!
A vampire survivors like that's mostly black and yellow with a few other colors. You play on your skill tree and must navigate to on it to gain more skills.
Very early into your first run, you can encounter a crab enemy.
No descriptions of your abilities makes this a bit of a chore, though I don't think fixing that would cause me to start enjoying this. Pretty plain for a survivors game.
